title: The Bridge of Port Mahon
premise: In 1911, Edmund Iversen drives for the fiery suffragist Adeline Marsh, reading her correspondence and keeping his own history sealed inside a locked satchel. When a census taker's probing questions expose that his papers name three people who no longer exist, Edmund realizes the authorities are closing in on the forged identities he built to smuggle his family out of political persecution years ago. As war rumors swell and the last ship from Port Mahon prepares to sail, he must decide which of his scattered found family—the suffragists who became his people, or the sister who never stopped waiting—gets the final berth. He gives up his own place, sending them across the water while he stays behind to face the inquiry, discovering that memory, faithfully kept, is its own kind of survival.
about_author: Z. M. Brightwater is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing emigration records in Mediterranean port towns. Their fiction has appeared in small literary journals under other names; this is their first novel.

chapters.title: The Weight of Letters
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. We meet him steaming open and resealing Adeline Marsh's mail each night, memorizing lives he'll never live. He catalogs what can be carried: one satchel, two photographs, a brass key. Emotional beat: quiet longing disguised as professional habit.

chapters.title: The Census Man
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. A polite census taker named Mr. Quill visits the Marsh household and asks about 'other residents.' Edmund lies smoothly, but Quill writes something down anyway. Emotional beat: first crack in the armor of invisibility.

chapters.title: Adeline's War
chapters.summary: Adeline's POV. She plans a rally, oblivious to Edmund's dread, and reveals a flash of tenderness toward her driver she'd never voice aloud. Emotional beat: the suffragist cause as both shield and exposure.

chapters.title: The Satchel
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, flashback-heavy. The origin of his forged identity: the night in 1900 he carried his sister Marta and her children past checkpoints using papers meant for the dead. Emotional beat: guilt braided with pride.

chapters.title: Port Mahon at Dusk
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, rotating brief POVs among household staff. The harbor town hums with naval buildup; ships are being requisitioned. Emotional beat: collective unease, the sense of a clock starting.

chapters.title: Marta's Letter
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The letter from Chapter 1 was from Marta: she's alive, destitute, and asking to come to him—a journey requiring papers he no longer dares forge. Emotional beat: joy curdling into arithmetic.

chapters.title: Quill Returns
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Quill interviews him formally about 'discrepancies' in prior census records. Edmund realizes someone reported him. Emotional beat: paranoia; every kindness now reads as surveillance.

chapters.title: What Adeline Carries
chapters.summary: Adeline's POV. Arrested briefly after a rally, she bails herself out and finds Edmund waiting with the car running. Their first true conversation. Emotional beat: found family crystallizing under pressure.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Berths
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. He counts: Marta, her two children, himself—one berth short even before considering Adeline's household. He begins forging again, hands shaking. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Watched
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV (a stable boy Edmund mentors). Tomas sees Edmund burning documents and draws the wrong conclusion—that Edmund is a spy. Emotional beat: innocence as hazard.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Candlelight
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Quill confronts him with the burned paper's fragments and the 1900 passenger manifest. Edmund performs ignorance brilliantly—but Quill leaves a photograph on the table: young Edmund, Marta, the dock. Emotional beat: terror held behind courtesy.

chapters.title: Confession at the Kitchen Table
chapters.summary: Dual POV, Edmund and Adeline. He tells her everything. Instead of betrayal she laughs—then weeps—then starts planning. Emotional beat: relief of being known; found family tested and holding.

chapters.title: The Harbormaster's Price
chapters.summary: Adeline's POV. She negotiates for two berths, not four. The price: her movement's funds, crippling the cause she's built her life around. Emotional beat: sacrifice measured against conviction.

chapters.title: Marta Arrives Early
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Marta appears at the door unannounced, half-starved, with only one child—her son died on the road. Grief and reunion collide. Emotional beat: memory as wound and anchor.

chapters.title: Three Names for One Man
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Quill catches Edmund mid-errand and offers a deal: betray Adeline's network, keep his freedom. Edmund sees the trap's elegance—it was never about him. Emotional beat: temptation framed as mercy.

chapters.title: The Night of Forged Ink
chapters.summary: Ensemble. The household works through the night producing documents for Marta and her daughter, Adeline forging with surprising skill learned from arrested comrades. Emotional beat: solidarity as resistance.

chapters.title: Which One Gets the Last Berth
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, the moral climax approached. Marta demands the berth; so does Adeline, arguing the movement needs Marta's testimony abroad. Edmund must choose between blood and chosen family. Emotional beat: anguish distilled to a single decision.

chapters.title: The Last Sailing
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. He puts Marta and her daughter aboard, keeps the third berth empty rather than choose between Adeline and himself, and steps back onto the quay as the whistle blows. Emotional beat: heartbreak transfigured into resolve.

chapters.title: The Inquiry
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Interrogated at last, he refuses to give a single name, reciting instead the dead—his parents, Marta's son, the strangers whose papers he carried—until the room itself seems to mourn. Emotional beat: dignity as defiance.

chapters.title: What Quill Knew
chapters.summary: Quill's POV. His brother drowned because of the same regime that hunted Edmund; the investigation was penance, not duty. He releases Edmund with falsified papers. Emotional beat: unexpected grace between adversaries.

chapters.title: Letters Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, months later. War has come; Adeline's household endures. Marta's letters arrive from abroad, and for the first time Edmund reads one aloud to the whole table instead of silently. Emotional beat: memory transformed into inheritance.

chapters.title: The Bridge of Port Mahon
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, epilogue. Years later, an old man, he walks the rebuilt harbor bridge and greets a young refugee asking how to carry a life across water. He gives her the satchel. Emotional beat: the price of survival paid forward; found family outlasting all borders.
